6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end
181	
182	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/

48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt

60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

99	end DegAt

102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl

173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl

284	/-- **THE PROJECT'S CENTRAL OPEN OBLIGATION — expected to stay open.**
285	
286	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch`: for a smooth proper geometrically
287	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
288	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
289	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
290	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
291	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
292	why they are bundled.
293	
294	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
295	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
296	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
297	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
298	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
299	labelled as strictly weaker.
300	
301	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
302	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
303	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
304	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
305	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
306	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
307	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
308	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
309	
310	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
311	Discharging it means formalising the Kleiman §4 existence proof: the Abel-map
312	slice `Div^d_{C/k} → Pic^d_{C/k}` is a smooth proper equivalence relation whose
313	quotient is a scheme (`smoothProperQuotient`, itself gated on
314	`HasSmoothProperQuotient` because Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity
315	vocabulary), together with `Div` representability (Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`,
316	which needs the Quot scheme). Neither input is available; the project reaches
317	this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single named `sorry` that
318	the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with a weaker
319	conditional statement to make a count go down.
320	
321	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
322	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
323	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison class
324	`PicEtComparisonIso` and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is
325	derived from it.
326	
327	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
328	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
329	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
330	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
331	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
332	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
333	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
334	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
335	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
336	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
337	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
338	than asserting it. -/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf

9	/-!
10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
11	
12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
17	
18	## Main declarations
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
24	  representation it induces.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
35	  supplies.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
40	
41	## The hypothesis bundle
42	
43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
50	-/
51

55	universe u

57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
58	
59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
60	
61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
66	
67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
74	    JacobianData C where
75	  J := J
76	  rep := rep
77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
78	  quasiCompact := hqc
79	
80	@[simp]
81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
85	  rfl
86	
87	@[simp]
88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
92	  rfl
93	
94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
95	@[simp]
96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
104	
105	section Charts
106	
107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
109	
110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
115	
116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
118	
119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
126	
127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
130	
131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
137	
138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
147	  exact h.symm
148	
149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
150	
151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
158	  have h := hlft i
159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
160	
161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
171	
172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
201	
202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
212	    JacobianData C :=
213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
223	  rfl
224	
225	end Charts

227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
8	
9	/-!
10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
11	
12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
17	
18	## Main declarations
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
24	  representation it induces.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
35	  supplies.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
40	
41	## The hypothesis bundle
42	
43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
50	-/
51	
52	set_option autoImplicit false
53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
54	
55	universe u
56	
57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
58	
59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
60	
61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
66	
67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
74	    JacobianData C where
75	  J := J
76	  rep := rep
77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
78	  quasiCompact := hqc
79	
80	@[simp]
81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
85	  rfl
86	
87	@[simp]
88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
92	  rfl
93	
94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
95	@[simp]
96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
104	
105	section Charts
106	
107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
109	
110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
115	
116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
118	
119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
126	
127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
130	
131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
137	
138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
147	  exact h.symm
148	
149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
150	
151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
158	  have h := hlft i
159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
160	
161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
171	
172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
201	
202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
212	    JacobianData C :=
213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
223	  rfl
224	
225	end Charts
226	
227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry

40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory
43	
44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
45	
46	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
47	
48	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/
53	
54	namespace PicEtAff
55	
56	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
57	
58	/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
59	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
60	  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
61	  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
62	  left_inv x := by
63	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
64	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
65	    exact mapAlg_id C x
66	  right_inv x := by
67	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
68	      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
69	    exact mapAlg_id C x
70	  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y
71	
72	@[simp]
73	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
74	    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
75	  rfl
76	
77	@[simp]
78	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
79	    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
80	  rfl
81	
82	end PicEtAff
83	
84	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
85	
86	variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
87	
88	/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
89	the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
90	restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
91	def picEtSubgroup :
92	    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
93	  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
94	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
95	  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
96	  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
97	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
98	  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]
99	
100	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
101	level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
102	`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
103	tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
104	canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
105	def picEt : Type u :=
106	  picEtSubgroup C T
107	
108	noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
109	  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))
110	
111	namespace picEt
112	
113	variable {C T}
114	
115	/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
116	lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
117	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
118	  s.2 U V h
119	
120	@[ext]
121	lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
122	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
123	
124	variable (C T) in
125	/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
126	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
127	  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
128	    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype
129	
130	@[simp]
131	lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
132	  rfl
133	
134	@[simp]
135	lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
136	    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
141	  rfl
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=
145	  rfl
146	
147	end picEt
148	
149	/-! ## The affine comparison -/
150	
151	section Affine
152	
153	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
154	
155	/-- The top affine open of an affine test object. -/
156	def overSpecTopAffine : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens :=
157	  ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A⟩
158	
159	/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
160	`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
161	comparison. -/
162	def picEtToAff : picEt C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A :=
163	  (PicEtAff.congr C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A)).toMonoidHom.comp
164	    (picEt.eval C (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
165	
166	lemma picEtToAff_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
167	    picEtToAff C A s
168	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
169	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	/-- The section of `picEt` over an affine test determined by a plus class of the test
173	algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse direction of the affine
174	comparison. -/
175	def picEtOfAff : PicEtAff C A →* picEt C (overSpec k A) where

93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]
113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData
147	
148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
157	
158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
159	
160	open MonObj
161	
162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicRepDatum
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataAbelSurj
8	
9	/-!
10	# DJ-IN — the DAT-G → DAT-J handoff: a `PicRepDatum` at the challenge field is a `JacobianData`
11	
12	`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md` §1.1/§0.9 pins the interface DAT-J consumes from DAT-G as
13	**DJ-IN** = `PicRepDatum k k C`, and its §1.1 producer target reads
14	
15	```
16	jacobianData C : JacobianData C where
17	  J := (datGDatum C).J ; rep := (datGDatum C).rep
18	  locallyOfFiniteType := (datGDatum C).lft ; quasiCompact := quasiCompact_jacobian C
19	```
20	
21	with the note that *"every symbol on the RHS except `datGDatum` (DAT-G) and
22	`quasiCompact_jacobian` (DJ-1) is landed"* and that the `rep :=` line needs **no adapter**
23	because the two field types are definitionally equal (`Picard/PicRepDatum.lean`, the module's
24	defeq smoke test).
25	
26	That packaging had never been written.  `PicRepDatum` occurs in no other Lean file in the
27	tree: the defeq is recorded as an `example`, so nothing *consumes* it, and DAT-J's assembly
28	was left as the pair (DAT-G output, qc) with no term joining them.  This file writes it.
29	
30	The content is exactly the interface, so it is short by design — but it is not nothing:
31	writing it is what turns "DAT-G produces a datum over `k'`, and separately DAT-J wants one
32	over `k`" into a single arrow, and it is what makes the remaining DAT-J debt *visibly* two
33	statements (the DAT-G descent, and the quasi-compactness) rather than an unspecified
34	assembly.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianData` — DJ-IN: a `PicRepDatum k k C` plus
39	  quasi-compactness of its representing object is a `JacobianData C`, with `J`, `rep` and
40	  `lft` carried across unchanged.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianData_J` / `_rep` — the two projections, `rfl`, so
42	  a consumer never unfolds the packaging.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` — the same with quasi-compactness
44	  supplied in the shape the classical argument delivers it: per-point residue-field lifts of
45	  an Abel morphism out of `DivScheme g` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`).
46	
47	## What this does NOT do
48	
49	It produces no `PicRepDatum`.  That is DAT-G/DAT-G0 — the finite-Galois descent from a
50	finite separable stage, whose one avatar-less core is `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`
51	(`Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean`), and it is divRep-gated.  Nor does it produce the
52	quasi-compactness or an Abel lift.  What it removes is the *assembly* step between them.
53	-/
54	
55	set_option autoImplicit false
56	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
57	
58	universe u
59	
60	open CategoryTheory Limits

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
8	
9	/-!
10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
11	
12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
17	
18	## Main declarations
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
24	  representation it induces.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
35	  supplies.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
40	
41	## The hypothesis bundle
42	
43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
50	-/
51	
52	set_option autoImplicit false
53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
54	
55	universe u
56	
57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
58	
59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
60	
61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
66	
67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
74	    JacobianData C where
75	  J := J
76	  rep := rep
77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
78	  quasiCompact := hqc
79	
80	@[simp]
81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
85	  rfl
86	
87	@[simp]
88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
92	  rfl
93	
94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
95	@[simp]
96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
104	
105	section Charts
106	
107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
109	
110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
115	
116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
118	
119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
126	
127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
130	
131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
137	
138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
147	  exact h.symm
148	
149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
150	
151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
158	  have h := hlft i
159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
160	
161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
171	
172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
201	
202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
212	    JacobianData C :=
213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
223	  rfl
224	
225	end Charts
226	
227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry
