9	/-!
10	# The Abel chart map of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
11	
12	`JacobianData.ofCharts` consumes a family of morphisms of big-site presheaves
13	`yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C`.  This file builds such a morphism out of the two
14	things the tree already has: the Abel transformation of divisor families into the degree-zero
15	Picard functor on the slice, and a representation of the divisor functor by a scheme.
16	
17	The passage from the slice to the big site is the Σ-extension, and it is functorial in two
18	independent ways, both established here in the general categorical setting:
19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat` — the Σ-extension is functorial in the extended
21	  presheaf: a natural transformation `F ⟶ G` of presheaves on the slice `Over S` induces one
22	  of presheaves on the ambient category.
23	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.toSigmaExtension` — a representation of `F` by an
24	  object `J` of the slice induces a morphism `yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F` from the
25	  ambient yoneda presheaf of the underlying object.  A point of `J.left` over a test `V` is a
26	  map `v : V ⟶ J.left`, and it names the Σ-element whose structure morphism is `v ≫ J.hom` and
27	  whose fibre component is the universal element pulled back along `v`.
28	
29	Composing the second with the first at the Abel transformation gives the chart map.
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValueTrans` — **the Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard
34	  functor**: under the chart-index degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value
35	  `abelDiv s · sigmaFamily Z · (θ^m)⁻¹` of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` is a natural transformation
36	  `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.  Naturality is `picEtMap_chartValue`, membership is
37	  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChart` — **the Abel chart map**: given a representation of the
39	  divisor functor by a scheme `D` over `k` (a section variable — this file never constructs
40	  one), the morphism of big-site presheaves
41	  `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` sending a `D`-point to the class of the divisor
42	  family it names, twisted into degree zero.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_abelSigmaChart` — the structure morphism of the single chart of
44	  this family is the structure morphism of the representing object, so the chart hypothesis
45	  `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` of `JacobianData.ofCharts` is exactly
46	  `LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` for it.
47	
48	## What this is NOT
49	
50	This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
51	`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
52	tree today:
53	
54	* `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
55	  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
56	  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It
57	  becomes an open immersion only after restricting to the open locus where the fibre is a single
58	  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3.
59	
60	  Two updates to this bullet, both 2026-07-29.  `chartLocus` **now exists in Lean**
61	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`, and open at a general test unconditionally), so the closing
62	  clause above — that it does not — is stale.  And the implication "not a monomorphism, hence
63	  not `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`" is a **derivation**, not an extra fact: it is
64	  `mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` (`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean`), from
65	  mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  The same file gives
66	  the criterion that makes the restricted statement provable, and
67	  `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` instantiates it here.
68	* `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc …)` is the statement that
69	  every degree-zero class is Zariski-locally the twisted class of a divisor family in the
70	  window.  Over a field this is Riemann–Roch; the relative statement is DAT-B's coverage row.
71	-/

50	This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
51	`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
52	tree today:

55	  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
56	  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It
57	  becomes an open immersion only after restricting to the open locus where the fibre is a single
58	  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3.

17	  J := (datGDatum C).J ; rep := (datGDatum C).rep
18	  locallyOfFiniteType := (datGDatum C).lft ; quasiCompact := quasiCompact_jacobian C
19	```
20

22	`quasiCompact_jacobian` (DJ-1) is landed"* and that the `rep :=` line needs **no adapter**
23	because the two field types are definitionally equal (`Picard/PicRepDatum.lean`, the module's
24	defeq smoke test).
25	
26	That packaging had never been written.  `PicRepDatum` occurs in no other Lean file in the
27	tree: the defeq is recorded as an `example`, so nothing *consumes* it, and DAT-J's assembly
28	was left as the pair (DAT-G output, qc) with no term joining them.  This file writes it.
29	
30	The content is exactly the interface, so it is short by design — but it is not nothing:
31	writing it is what turns "DAT-G produces a datum over `k'`, and separately DAT-J wants one
32	over `k`" into a single arrow, and it is what makes the remaining DAT-J debt *visibly* two
33	statements (the DAT-G descent, and the quasi-compactness) rather than an unspecified
34	assembly.

39	  quasi-compactness of its representing object is a `JacobianData C`, with `J`, `rep` and
40	  `lft` carried across unchanged.

42	  a consumer never unfolds the packaging.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` — the same with quasi-compactness
44	  supplied in the shape the classical argument delivers it: per-point residue-field lifts of
45	  an Abel morphism out of `DivScheme g` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`).

52	quasi-compactness or an Abel lift.  What it removes is the *assembly* step between them.

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf

/-!
# The open-immersion evaluation bridge (DAT-6, stage 1)

The Zariski sheaf property of `picEt`/`pic0` landed by DAT-2
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf`) speaks *topological* covers of the test:
open sets `O i ⊆ T.left` and local data valued at affine opens subordinate to them.
The 01JJ packaging (DAT-6 stages 2–3) speaks *morphism-form* covers: families
`f i : T' i ⟶ T` of test morphisms with open-immersion left legs, jointly surjective,
carrying sections `x i : picEt C (T' i)` compatible on all common refinements.  This
file is the bridge: it evaluates a morphism-form family into DAT-2's `picEt.LocalData`
on the ranges `O i := (f i).left.opensRange` and exports the sheaf property of `picEt`
and of its degree-zero subfunctor in morphism-cover form.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.appLEAlgEquiv`: the section-ring isomorphism of an open
  immersion of tests, `Γ(T.left, V) ≃ₐ[k] Γ(T'.left, f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)` for
  `V ≤ opensRange`, upgrading `Over.appLEAlgHom` (bijectivity:
  `Over.bijective_appLEAlgHom`, from `Scheme.Hom.isIso_app`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.coverValue`: the value at an affine open `W` subordinate to
  a cover member of the section carried by that member — evaluate at the preimage
  affine open and transport back along `appLEAlgEquiv`.  It is local data:
  `coverValue_res` (restriction within a member, pure `appLE`/`res` calculus) and
  `coverValue_glue` (agreement across members at a shared affine open, through the
  mediating test `picEt.overlapTest` — the open subscheme of the target at `W` — and
  `IsOpenImmersion.lift`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.ext_of_cover` / `picEt.existsUnique_of_cover`: **the sheaf
  property of `picEt` in morphism-cover form** — separation and unique gluing for a
  compatible family on an abstract open-immersion cover of the test.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover` /
  `pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`: the same for the degree-zero subfunctor;
  membership of the glued section is DAT-2's S-lemma (`mem_pic0Subgroup_of_cover`).

The compatibility hypothesis is the morphism form (`Presieve.Arrows.Compatible`
transported to the slice): for every pair of members and every test `Z` mapping to
both compatibly, the two restrictions of the family agree.  Stage 3 instantiates it
from a compatible family of elements of the Σ-extension on a scheme-level open cover.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-! ## The section-ring isomorphism of an open immersion of tests -/

namespace Over

90	
91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
93	
94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
97	covering sieve is covering.
98	
99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
114	
115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
116	
117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
122	
123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataCharts
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeAbel
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Abel chart map of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
11	
12	`JacobianData.ofCharts` consumes a family of morphisms of big-site presheaves
13	`yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C`.  This file builds such a morphism out of the two
14	things the tree already has: the Abel transformation of divisor families into the degree-zero
15	Picard functor on the slice, and a representation of the divisor functor by a scheme.
16	
17	The passage from the slice to the big site is the Σ-extension, and it is functorial in two
18	independent ways, both established here in the general categorical setting:
19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat` — the Σ-extension is functorial in the extended
21	  presheaf: a natural transformation `F ⟶ G` of presheaves on the slice `Over S` induces one
22	  of presheaves on the ambient category.
23	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.toSigmaExtension` — a representation of `F` by an
24	  object `J` of the slice induces a morphism `yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F` from the
25	  ambient yoneda presheaf of the underlying object.  A point of `J.left` over a test `V` is a
26	  map `v : V ⟶ J.left`, and it names the Σ-element whose structure morphism is `v ≫ J.hom` and
27	  whose fibre component is the universal element pulled back along `v`.
28	
29	Composing the second with the first at the Abel transformation gives the chart map.
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValueTrans` — **the Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard
34	  functor**: under the chart-index degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value
35	  `abelDiv s · sigmaFamily Z · (θ^m)⁻¹` of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` is a natural transformation
36	  `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.  Naturality is `picEtMap_chartValue`, membership is
37	  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChart` — **the Abel chart map**: given a representation of the
39	  divisor functor by a scheme `D` over `k` (a section variable — this file never constructs
40	  one), the morphism of big-site presheaves
41	  `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` sending a `D`-point to the class of the divisor
42	  family it names, twisted into degree zero.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_abelSigmaChart` — the structure morphism of the single chart of
44	  this family is the structure morphism of the representing object, so the chart hypothesis
45	  `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` of `JacobianData.ofCharts` is exactly
46	  `LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` for it.
47	
48	## What this is NOT
49	
50	This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
51	`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
52	tree today:
53	
54	* `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
55	  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
56	  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It
57	  becomes an open immersion only after restricting to the open locus where the fibre is a single
58	  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3.
59	
60	  Two updates to this bullet, both 2026-07-29.  `chartLocus` **now exists in Lean**
61	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`, and open at a general test unconditionally), so the closing
62	  clause above — that it does not — is stale.  And the implication "not a monomorphism, hence
63	  not `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`" is a **derivation**, not an extra fact: it is
64	  `mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` (`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean`), from
65	  mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  The same file gives
66	  the criterion that makes the restricted statement provable, and
67	  `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` instantiates it here.
68	* `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc …)` is the statement that
69	  every degree-zero class is Zariski-locally the twisted class of a divisor family in the
70	  window.  Over a field this is Riemann–Roch; the relative statement is DAT-B's coverage row.
71	-/

74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

78	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

80	/-! ## Σ-extension plumbing (general category theory)
81	
82	Both constructions below are stated for presheaves valued in `Type v`, the hom-universe of the
83	ambient category, because that is where the ambient yoneda presheaf lives and the Σ-extension
84	must meet it. -/

86	namespace CategoryTheory
87	
88	namespace Over
89	
90	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F G : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
91	
92	/-- **The Σ-extension is functorial in the extended presheaf**: a natural transformation of
93	presheaves on the slice induces one of their Σ-extensions, acting as the identity on the
94	structure-morphism component. -/
95	def sigmaExtensionNat (φ : F ⟶ G) : sigmaExtension S F ⟶ sigmaExtension S G where
96	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun x => ⟨x.1, φ.app _ x.2⟩
97	  naturality T T' g := by
98	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_
99	    obtain ⟨a, ξ⟩ := x
100	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk (g.unop ≫ a))
101	      (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (φ.naturality (Over.homMk g.unop rfl :
102	        Over.mk (g.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op) ξ)
103	
104	@[simp]
105	lemma sigmaExtensionNat_app_fst (φ : F ⟶ G) (T : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (sigmaExtension S F).obj T) :
106	    ((sigmaExtensionNat φ).app T x).1 = x.1 :=
107	  rfl
108	
109	end Over
